name: Breastfeeding benefits (breast pump coverage)
whatYouGet: Most health plans must cover a breast pump (rental or purchase) plus breastfeeding support and counseling, per the HealthCare.gov breastfeeding benefits page.
costDetail: Covered without cost-sharing under qualifying plans
eligibility: People with a health plan subject to the ACA preventive-services rule (Marketplace and most other plans; grandfathered plans are exempt)
catches: Plans may set rules on manual vs electric, rental length, and timing (before or after birth); some require doctor preauthorization.
notes: Not fetched directly (site unreachable from this session); details come from an official-domain search result. Check your plan or insurer for specifics. Step-by-step claim tips not yet verified.

name: Qualify for a Free Breast Pump Through Insurance
whatYouGet: Supplier that checks your insurance and ships a covered breast pump if your plan includes one.
costDetail: No cost if your plan covers the pump; upgrade models may carry a fee
eligibility: People whose health plan covers a breast pump; coverage, timing and prescription rules vary by plan
catches: Usually one pump per pregnancy; some plans need a prescription or preauthorization; upgrade fees may apply. Supplier will contact your insurer.
notes: Search result says you can apply during pregnancy and up to one year after delivery. Claim tips: 1) Call the number on your insurance card to confirm pump coverage, models, prescription and timing. 2) Use the supplier's online form to check coverage. 3) Supplier verifies benefits and handles paperwork. 4) Get a prescription if your plan requires one. 5) Order once your plan allows (some ship only near the due date). Only one supplier per pregnancy. Site not fetched; backed by official-domain search results.

name: WIC (Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children)
whatYouGet: Nutrition support for pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants and children under 5, delivered through local WIC agencies.
costDetail: Free; apply through a local WIC agency
eligibility: Pregnant, postpartum or breastfeeding women, infants and children up to age 5 who meet income limits (generally at or below 185% of poverty; SNAP, Medicaid or TANF participation can meet this), live in the state, and are at nutritional risk.
catches: Appointment at a local agency and a free health check are required.
notes: Online pre-screening tool only checks likely eligibility; it is not an application. States may set lower income limits. The official 'how to apply' page was not confirmed; signupUrl is the eligibility page. Not fetched directly; backed by official-domain search results.

name: Medicaid and CHIP pregnancy coverage
whatYouGet: Medicaid covers pregnancy-related care at least through 60 days postpartum; some states cover 12 months. CHIP can cover pregnant people in some states, and newborns of enrolled mothers are generally covered automatically.
eligibility: Income-based; limits vary by state (see CMS eligibility-levels table).
notes: Apply through your state Medicaid agency or HealthCare.gov. Some figures seen may be outdated. Not fetched directly; backed by official-domain search results.

name: PSI HelpLine
whatYouGet: Free, confidential helpline for support and resources on perinatal mental health; call or text 800-944-4773 (English; Spanish text 971-203-7773).
catches: Not for emergencies; messages are returned by volunteers (up to 48 hours).
notes: In crisis: 988 or National Maternal Mental Health Hotline 1-833-852-6262. Not fetched directly; backed by official-domain search results.

whatYouGet: Early Head Start programs may serve pregnant women and expectant families.
